- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak or adjust downward 1–2 days after spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and model is overconfidently bullish, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (especially 20–30 days out); add 1–3% to forecast tail (last 5–7 days) to account for momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for stability.
